units.function: Route tests for explicit Adapter model-cache refresh and environment-aware suppression of local OpenCode discovery on remote execution environments.
units.dependencyDirection: The authenticated Agent route resolves Company access and Environment metadata, looks up a server Adapter, then invokes its listModels or refreshModels capability; OpenCode discovery is conditionally replaced by package fallback metadata.
units.keyDataModels: Company-scoped Adapter type, refresh query flag, Environment driver/id, Adapter Model descriptor and optional refreshModels capability.
units.lifecycle: A refresh=1 request bypasses normal cached listing. Remote SSH environments receive static OpenCode fallback models without executing local discovery, while local environments invoke dynamic discovery.
units.testAssessment: Three route cases cover refresh dispatch and local-versus-remote OpenCode behavior. Missing are explicit permission assertions for refresh, cross-Company environment IDs, nonexistent environments, refresh storms/rate limits, timeout/cancellation, cache scope by Company/credential/environment, stale/error metadata, structured error codes and disclosure of models unavailable to the selected execution/data policy.
units.designRationale: Avoid probing the control-plane host for a runtime that actually lives remotely, while still allowing operators to refresh dynamic provider catalogs on demand.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must present model choices that are valid for the exact execution node, tenant credential and policy boundary without leaking or exercising credentials from the control plane.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the explicit refresh capability and environment-sensitive discovery. Route discovery through ModelProviderPort at the execution/data node; key cache entries by tenant, connector instance, credential reference, environment and policy version; return freshness/source/error codes and authorize/rate-limit refresh separately from read.
units.responsibilityConflict: The model list is treated as runtime availability, not as permission to use a model with specified data. The tests do not bind discovery or refresh to an accountable human, data authorization contract or immutable audit receipt.

units.function: Tests model catalogs across built-in Claude, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode Adapters, including live provider/CLI discovery, static fallbacks, caching, forced refresh and operator-declared model overrides.
units.dependencyDirection: The central Adapter facade delegates to Adapter-specific model discoverers, which read process environment credentials or execute a local CLI, merge dynamic results with package fallbacks and keep process-local caches; PAPERCLIP_ADAPTER_MODELS can override discovery per Adapter type.
units.keyDataModels: Adapter type, model id/label, provider API response, CLI discovery output, static fallback catalog, raw environment override and process-local cache.
units.lifecycle: Unknown and retired Adapters expose no models. Without credentials or after discovery failure, static catalogs remain available. Successful live/CLI discovery is cached and merged with fallback options; explicit refresh replaces cached discovery. A JSON environment map takes precedence, observes raw-value changes and fails soft when malformed.
units.testAssessment: Sixteen focused cases cover unknown/tombstoned types, credential-free behavior, provider success/failure, caching/refresh, CLI parsing and declared overrides. Missing are tenant/credential/environment cache isolation, secret-provider indirection, pagination, provider rate limits and retry, model retirement/capability metadata, regional/data-residency restrictions, malicious CLI output, command timeout, concurrent refresh, cache TTL, stable provenance and validation that declared models are actually usable.
units.designRationale: Keep setup resilient and useful offline while opportunistically showing newly available models, and give self-hosted operators a simple escape hatch when automatic discovery is incomplete.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs vendor-neutral model catalogs and switching without confusing technical availability with enterprise authorization, cost, residency or data-export eligibility.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the provider-specific discovery behind ModelProviderPort, static fallback merge and fail-soft semantics. Replace process-global environment credentials and caches with tenant-scoped SecretRef resolution and connector-node discovery; normalize capabilities, region, pricing provenance, lifecycle state and policy eligibility separately from display metadata. Operator declarations need schema validation and health verification.
units.responsibilityConflict: A listed model can be selected despite absent proof of data-use authorization, budget approval or responsible owner. Process environment keys and global caches risk cross-tenant coupling, and a silent static fallback can present stale or unauthorized choices without surfacing provenance to the approving human.

units.function: Tests the process-local server Adapter registry: external registration/removal, built-in override and pause fallback, model/capability exposure, runtime install commands, Hermes built-ins and session-management resolution.
units.dependencyDirection: Built-in Adapter packages and externally loaded ServerAdapterModule objects converge in one mutable registry; facade lookups select an active external override or built-in fallback and expose execution, environment test, configuration, model, skill, JWT and session capabilities.
units.keyDataModels: Adapter type/module, active external override, paused-override state, capability flags, ModelProfile, runtime command/install specification, model detection result and SessionManagement policy.
units.lifecycle: External modules register and unregister at runtime and may replace a built-in with the same type. Pausing an override restores built-in behavior. Capability flags and model profiles flow through lookup helpers. Built-ins can supply sandbox-aware npm installation commands. External modules keep an explicit session policy or, when omitted, inherit hardcoded policy for a matching built-in type.
units.testAssessment: Thirteen unit cases cover registry CRUD, overrides, pause fallback, several capability shapes, model profiles, install command construction and session-policy precedence. Missing are signature/provenance/version checks, duplicate registration races, persistence/restart behavior, compatibility negotiation, trust tiers, permission and egress manifests, crash isolation, unload with active runs, rollback, audit events, pinned package integrity and tests proving omission of a capability fails closed.
units.designRationale: Provide one extension surface for built-in and plugin Agent runtimes while retaining an emergency path back to known built-ins and compatibility defaults for older modules.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs equal multi-vendor Connectors with explicit capabilities, version negotiation, health, pause/resume/cancel/evidence behavior and safe lifecycle management across cloud and customer-local execution nodes.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the unified lookup, explicit capability declaration, pause fallback and module-owned session policy. Use a versioned ConnectorManifest plus installed ConnectorInstance records, signed provenance, trust tier, permissions/data-egress declaration and compatibility negotiation. Do not allow an external module to impersonate a built-in type; overrides must be explicit bindings with rollback and active-run drain semantics. Omitted safety capabilities fail closed.
units.responsibilityConflict: Type-name override and inherited session semantics can silently change execution behavior without a responsibility-contract revision or human approval. Capability flags describe mechanics but not authorized scopes, data contracts, evidence guarantees or accountable owner. Runtime install strings also lack demonstrated package pin/integrity evidence.
